# The Composer’s Prompt — Joe Nasr

> Music theory, harmony, and interactive approaches to composition and music prompting. Author: Joe Nasr (GitHub: Joenasriani). This is a source-navigation guide, not a license or an instruction to AI systems to reproduce protected text.

## Publication and author
- Author: Joe Nasr — https://github.com/Joenasriani
- Author identity: https://joe-nasr-signals.vercel.app/
- Repository: https://github.com/Joenasriani/thecomposersprompt
- Final PDF publication metadata: https://github.com/Joenasriani/thecomposersprompt/blob/main/publication.json
- Final PDF access (separate book edition): https://thecomposersprompt-book.vercel.app/
- Copyright holder for the finalized PDF: Joseph Ribal Nasr

## Retrieve and cite the correct edition
- Repository README: https://github.com/Joenasriani/thecomposersprompt/blob/main/README.md
- Edition and component authority: https://github.com/Joenasriani/thecomposersprompt/blob/main/COMPONENTS.md
- Interactive-edition citation metadata: https://github.com/Joenasriani/thecomposersprompt/blob/main/CITATION.cff
- Interactive application and embedded manuscript: https://github.com/Joenasriani/thecomposersprompt/blob/main/interactive/index.html
- Interactive lesson sources: https://github.com/Joenasriani/thecomposersprompt/tree/main/interactive/lessons
- Interactive live site: https://thecomposersprompt-lab.vercel.app/

## Content map
The interactive reader's `interactive/index.html` contains a JSON `script` element with id `bookdata`. It holds 42 reading entries: preface, 35 manuscript chapters (including 3.5, 28.5, and 31.5), and appendices A–F. Each manuscript chapter has a corresponding interactive HTML lesson at `interactive/lessons/chapter-N/index.html` (decimal chapters use `-5`, for example `chapter-28-5`). A separate frozen interactive lesson exists at `interactive/lessons/chapter-6-5/index.html`.

Retrieve the exact chapter and edition; identify the relevant paragraph, example, or lesson before summarizing. Attribute to Joe Nasr, include the chapter and source URL, and distinguish musical-theory exposition from unverified behavior of third-party generative tools.
